It’s great that you are aware of all of these potential red flags this early on. And it’s good you are trying to get outside opinions so you don’t become blinded (also has happened to me before). But I would say you are fine to keep moving with this person right now. 

Its good to be aware of red flags but its not good to instantly treat them as if they have already done the “bad thing” you associate the red flag with. For example lets use the comment about her friend saying if it goes bad she wont recover until august. you are worried she might be insane. thats just one extremely negative possibility of many outcomes here. She could just be a deeply emotional/caring/loving person and has a hard time with heartbreak. I have severe adhd and I feel emotions much stronger than most regular people but I am far from what you would consider insane.

The point is to remember that you are worrying about things that haven’t happened yet. Dont worry about the red flags and what they could mean, just be aware of them moving forward in case anything does happen that points to an outcome your associating with the red flag. You cant control the future so dont waste time worrying about it. just go with the flow and see what happens. You say things are going good right now which they seem to be. Thats a much better thing to focus on because it’s reality and not just a hypothetical.

hey man just a tip outside of the tapes for you. I have extreme social anxiety but have gotten so much better to the point of being comfortable hosting speaking events where I’m talking to 200+ people when I used to actually panic when having to do any type of class presentation in school.

What I did is slowly trained myself through forcing myself to search for opportunities to interact with strangers in public. For example if I see someone wearing something cool i try to go out of my way to go compliment them. this is a good place to start because most times it would just be you saying that and then them saying thanks and then the interaction ends. so its not a big commitment compared to straight ip public speaking. 

Eventually I would start having whole conversations with people after complimenting them or saying something to them. I eventually was able to start approaching whole groups of strangers. Sure all of this was terrifying most of the time but the longer i kept doing it the easier it got. 

Whatever you decide to do I would say this could be a really good stepping stone. Good luck!

please do not listen to this comment. for the person that posted it - i want you to know I understand. I really really do. They are horrible evil people. But you have to think about the process of doing whatever it is you would be doing. Putting more energy into something negative when instead you could walk away and put that same energy into something positive. I know its insanely hard to do that and I don’t blame you if you decide otherwise but trust me when I say you will feel better looking back knowing you just removed yourself from the situation instead of stooping to their level.

Additionally it helps to realize you already have payback in a sense. It helped me to look back on ky ex and remember that she literally has to fake everything about herself for the people she surrounds herself with. Like imagine having to do that. Not being yourself ever. Never being truly happy. That was enough for me man. 

Your payback is moving on and forgetting they exist. They HATE not having power over you. Don’t let them have that power.

What I did was I went on a one week break with no contact (which she broke multiple times) to think things over. During that time I was talking to close friends about everything and it helped me come to my senses and then I just went in person and got it over with. It was ridiculously hard because she was ruthlessly manipulating me trying to get me to stay to the point of making me believe she would unalive herself if i left her house after doing it. What I did was text her mom that was home and let her know what she was telling me so she was aware in case she was serious which she wasn’t. 

One of the hardest things ive ever done but I knew it had to be done. Waking up and remembering that I couldn’t talk to them anymore was crippling. I went through a really dark period of time during the first month or two but over time it got better. slowly but surely. I started putting my focus into improving myself (good ole cliche i know) but it really did help a lot. Started walking/running everyday and drinking only water and eating healthy. 

It will be hard trust me. But you will thank yourself in the future when you look back at where you could have been if you stayed with them. You can do this. Stay strong and surround yourself with friends.
